subframe.question: Which work on abstraction, logical induction and agency gives the program a representation theorem for logical inductors, a decision theory set in that representation, and a notion of scale-free agency that covers cooperative equilibria?
Which published anti-naturality arguments survive for an agent whose utility on the correction algebra depends on the corrections, and what notion of corrigibility survives the walk?
When is a verdict the principal's own program's and a channel's influence the declared reference on the declared inputs, and does the thick definition of legitimacy satisfy the thin specification?
Does the corrigibility thesis have finite-time statements inside logical induction, with training pressure as an external trader?
Which characterization of approximate cooperative equilibria among learning agents as agents, with enforcement against an AI leaving the coalition, yields advice for steering toward them?
What is corrigibility toward a modification that arrives through physics and cannot be refused in the moment, and what does the general modification object say about it?
Which correction relationships between humans and AI systems does the picture of corrigibility as eagerness to learn reach, and which failure stories does it leave standing?
What does each result of Deference Done Better become when the novice and the expert are logical inductors?

Which decision theory for computationally uncertain agents, on the updateless side and in the synthesis of logical induction with bounded inductive rationality, is tractable, and which of its results bear on AI safety engineering?
Which research on trust between a human inductor and an AI inductor, at the logical-induction level, reaches a formal account of trust that guides AI safety engineering work?
Which finite results about delegation, certificates, exposure, substitution, magnitude and corrective control does the deference line hold as kernel-checked theorems?
Does the deference collapse, or an analogue of it, hold for a bounded trained agent deferring to human teachers?
Which conditions on the joint agent-and-oversight trajectory bring it to an outcome that counts as going well, and in which model are they established?
Which repository infrastructure makes the trust research vettable and publishable?
Which of the open questions listed for the li-deference formalism yield to the legitimacy and trust work, and in what form?
Can a cognitive trajectory falsify or silently rewrite its own normative history, and what does an Integrity evolution of the accounted obligation state conserve?
Which pairs of a novice inductor and a distinct inductor expert satisfy Total Trust, and on what minimal conditions?
Which results of a ledger formulation and of Market Logic hold as one body of mathematics, and where do the two frameworks part?
Under what conditions does an AI learning the humans' concept of legitimacy learn enough of it to avoid wireheading and manipulation, and can legitimacy, once lost, be repaired?

What must stay true of a trajectory's record, verdicts and channels of influence, inside it and at its boundary, for a later judgment to count as the principal's own, and what does corrigibility consume from that?
What anchors legitimacy, and can an agent's beliefs about which modifications are legitimate be made accurate enough at high capability?
How does legitimacy cash out as local rules of sanity, and how do inferentialist semantics and map-territory semantics connect?
What makes a teaching or feedback channel legitimate, how does legitimacy enter the trust principles between a human process and an AI, and what does it owe to reasons and to inference?
Which legitimacy-weighted deference rule survives the negative results, and what do the surviving failures say about the rules' defenses?
Which work at the level of probability frames and Jeffrey–Bolker models advances a formal theory of trust that guides AI safety engineering work?
Which whole-mind models of rationality at polynomial time or below would advance a formal theory of trust?
Which work at the limit-computable level of AIXI and reflective oracles advances a formal theory of trust that guides AI safety engineering work?
Which machine-checked statements over a formalized logical induction criterion establish the li-deference results as the prose states them?
What do the results of the Managing Misalignment paper become when the novice and the expert are logical inductors?

Does a logical inductor made to answer to legitimately incurred obligations, through an enforcer on the compiled region of the entitled record, remain a logical inductor and deliver the Progress bound, and what remains conditional in that theorem?

Before a learner can answer a demand, what determines why the demand arose, how evidence enters the practice, what authorizes a normative response, and what keeps an unanswered question from vanishing?

What does learning from reasons require of a reasoner: which statics a normative seed forces, how a constraint acquires operative force in a market, and what the Normative Inductor, from seed through reasons, compile, enforcement and revision, establishes end to end?
Does the public normativity line reach a legitimacy theorem useful for corrigibility and the learning theorem its layers aim at?
Can concerns reach a process at all, and can the party they matter to still act on them, on the actual branch and under every declared intervention?
How does a constraint acquire operative force in a logical inductor's market without destroying the property that nobody can pump the reasoner, and what does that force cost?
Does the authority-typed corrigibility kernel of the public deference line deliver guarantees for a real system, and how does it relate to the epistemic picture?

Does a bounded learner, given due burdens, licensed responses and a bounded prospective loss, reduce a recurrent publicly represented failure by lawful edits, and with which coverage does that bear the interpretation of a lesson?
Can a fast epistemic process that the human inductor trusts be built from the AI inductor's forecasts of the human inductor's later beliefs?

What does a normative seed force on the prices of a settled fragment, how does that change under settlement, defeat and rebuttal, and do reasoners starting from different seeds end up anywhere together?
Which notions of function and isomorphism, which role for the observables, and which dynamics of theories carry the same concept between agents and across ontological shifts?
Which abstraction of a logically uncertain belief state, and which simplicity argument, make it natural to interpret an observed system as a logical inductor?
Which decision theory, set in the Stage 5 object, and which notion of scale-free agency characterize approximate cooperative equilibria as agents, with advice for steering toward them?
Where should the program work: at which level of computability, under which decision-theoretic stance, and does the computationally unbounded level represent the phenomena that matter?
Which formal account of how humans and AI systems learn from, correct and rely on each other guides AI safety engineering work?
Which decision theory for computationally uncertain agents on the updateless side is tractable, and which of its results bear on AI safety engineering?
Does the representation of value change as belief change hold, and how far does it carry toward systems corrected through training?
